candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance client-needs subcategory (6–12% of items); this item tests injury-prevention education and promotion of safer health behaviors.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Community injury-prevention education for traumatic spinal cord injury
candidate.educational_objective: Promote spinal cord injury prevention through consistent seat-belt use and appropriate protective equipment during activities with traumatic-injury risk.

options.A: Use seat belts consistently and use appropriate protective equipment for sports and other higher-risk activities
options.B: Spinal cord injury prevention is relevant only to industrial workers, not to the general public
options.C: Seat-belt use has no relationship to spinal cord injury risk in motor-vehicle crashes
options.D: Protective sports equipment is unnecessary because sports injuries are not recognized causes of spinal cord injury

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke guidance identifies motor-vehicle crashes and serious falls as major causes of spinal cord injury and identifies not wearing proper safety gear, including a seat belt or protective sports equipment, as a risk factor. Current NICHD spinal-cord-injury information likewise identifies motor-vehicle exposure as a risk context and states that seat-belt use reduces spinal cord injury risk. B falsely limits prevention to one occupational group. C and D contradict current NIH guidance.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current NIH sources directly support seat-belt use and appropriate protective equipment as relevant spinal-cord-injury prevention measures in recognized traumatic risk settings.
candidate.source_document_title: Spinal Cord Injury; How many people are affected by SCI?
candidate.source_locator: NINDS 'Spinal Cord Injury' → 'Who is more likely to get a spinal cord injury?': motor vehicle accidents and serious falls are the most common causes in the U.S.; other causes include sports injuries; risk factors include not wearing proper gear such as a seat belt or protective sports equipment. NICHD 'How many people are affected by SCI?' → 'Who is at risk for SCI?': driving/riding in a car is a risk context and seat-belt use reduces the possibility of spinal cord injury.
candidate.source_organization: National Institutes of Health — National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS), corroborated by Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD)
candidate.source_version_date: Current NINDS and NICHD web guidance accessed 2026-08-18
